memories.content: Use a flow diagram rather than a sequence table when alternate procedural branches lead to different outcomes.
Draw alternate branches and their resulting outcomes in the same flow diagram so readers can compare them at once.
The visual fidelity of a prototype may differ from its functional fidelity.
A flow diagram can make alternate branches and their different outcomes visible in one view.
HCI reviewers often skim prototype screens and interaction flow diagrams before reading the main text.
Readers can understand the overall branching shape of a procedure more quickly from a flow diagram than from rows read one at a time.
Redrawing a branching flow diagram after a procedural change usually takes longer than updating one row in a table.
Reviewers often inspect the proposal’s main visual before reading the procedural explanation in full.
HCI reviewers find it difficult to assess result reproducibility if the system version used in the field deployment is not disclosed.
Record changes in system configurations, field procedures, and data collection tools during deployment, along with their timestamps and rationales.
The history of deployment versions and configuration changes provides necessary evidence for interpreting results from different field sites.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate concerns. The reference addresses how branching procedures and prototypes should be presented and reviewed, including a maintenance tradeoff; the compared frame addresses deployment-version and change documentation for reproducibility and cross-site interpretation.

relations.reason: These reference-side memories split one underlying presentation claim across format choice, diagram composition, visibility, and comprehension benefit; the compared frame contains no corresponding claim.
relations.summary: Flow diagrams provide a one-view presentation of alternate procedural branches and outcomes that supports quicker comparison and understanding than rowwise sequence tables.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-only distinction about prototype evaluation, with no corresponding compared-side claim.
relations.summary: A prototype’s visual fidelity and functional fidelity may differ.

relations.reason: The reference-side memories restate the same visual-first review behavior at general and HCI-specific levels; the compared frame does not address review order.
relations.summary: Reviewers often inspect key proposal visuals before reading the full written explanation.

relations.reason: This is a separate reference-only maintenance tradeoff rather than another statement of the diagram’s comprehension benefit.
relations.summary: Updating a branching flow diagram after procedural change generally takes longer than changing a single table row.

relations.reason: The compared-side memories split one documentation policy across version disclosure, timestamped change records with rationales, and their evidentiary value; the reference frame has no corresponding claim.
relations.summary: Deployment versions and operational changes should be disclosed and historically recorded to support reproducibility and interpretation across field sites.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame calls for disclosed, timestamped deployment-version and configuration histories to support reproducibility and interpretation across field sites.
reports.reference_only: The reference favors flow diagrams for branching procedures, distinguishes visual from functional prototype fidelity, notes reviewers’ visual-first reading behavior, and identifies higher diagram-update effort.
